messages:
Maria: quick sync — thinking about a 'Safeguard Switchpoint Controller' for rollouts. goal: unify A/B pilot routing + automatic degrade when signals cross thresholds. want to align on interfaces and tradeoffs. :eyes:
Jordan: +1. want to confirm if this is central decisioning or a local agent that observes and acts?
Tess: leaning local agent with a small central policy server. local can act faster on latency spikes; central coordinates global heuristics and TTLs.
Ryan: tradeoff is state sync. local agents will need consistent policy blobs and probe windows. how do we avoid thrashing (flip-flop) during noisy metrics?
Maria: we should add hysteresis and a minimum 'hold' period. proposal: `hold_ms`, `probe_window_s`, `consecutive_violations`.
Meera: also include a cheap health probe (no KV cache warmup) and a heavier sample (full path) for accuracy. separate the probe types in the interface.
Jordan: sounds good. also need to define the observable contract — which metrics must be available locally: p50/p95 latency, error_count, success_rate, token_tail_latency.
Tess: +1 on contract. suggest we expose a single derived signal `degradation_score` from the runtime so controller doesn't have to compute complex things. controller can combine it with traffic fraction and tier metadata.
Ryan: curious about session affinity implications. if we switch the upstream model variant or route to fallback, KV caches break cold. do we allow sticky-affinity per session and avoid switching that session unless critical?
Maria: yes — default: respect affinity for X minutes, but allow forced cutover after `emergency_threshold` breaches. add `eviction_strategy` for caches: `graceful_drain|immediate`.
Meera: for multi-tenant Dedicated customers, they may want a per-tenant policy override. how do we scope policies? per-tenant -> per-route -> global fallback. precedence should be explicit.
Jordan: agreed. policy precedence: route > tenant > global. control plane must serve a merged policy blob to agents.
Tess: what about rollback vs gradual switchover? controller should support `switch_mode: immediate|gradual|mirrored`. mirrored mode mirrors a % of calls for comparison (shadow) then flips.
Ryan: need safety budget for gradual flips: `max_delta_per_minute` and an emergency circuit that stops flips if errors spike. also keep rollout observability: event stream with decisions and reasons.
Maria: logs should include the decision trace and the metrics snapshot. short lines ok for UI. example: `DECIDE switchpoint=0.42 -> fallback; reasons=[p95>300ms x3, error_rate>2%]`.
Meera: we also need idempotent APIs for agents. e.g., POST /policy-apply {policy_id, generation, signature}. agents should ack and report generation they’re running.
Jordan: deployment bot FYI — we'll attempt a dogfood rollout after this sync. @deploy-bot start staging-canary now? :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: started workflow `staging-canary` for `switchpoint-controller` (run id 2026-171125). logs: https://ci.local/runs/2026-171125
Tess: one more ops concern — cost signal. fallback to smaller model reduces cost but may increase latency. we need a cost-utility term in the decision surface. recommend `utility = w1*latency_penalty + w2*cost_savings + w3*quality_regret`.
Ryan: concrete: include a tunable default vector, but allow tenant overrides. the UI should surface simulated outcomes for a policy change.
Maria: next steps: draft a tiny proto for the policy blob and a minimal local agent state machine. I'll drop a PR with YAML example. anyone want to pair?
Jordan: I can pair on the proto.
Tess: Me on the agent state machine.
Meera: I'll write the telemetry contract doc.
Maria: cool — thanks. follow up: add a short playbook for oncall that describes quick manual cutover steps and audit queries. I'll create the doc and ping infra. :thumbsup:
Ryan: thanks — great sync.
Maria: marking action items in the design tracker. good catch on cache eviction strategies.
Jordan: leaving notes: avoid central single point of failure, make policy fetch fallback-friendly, add backoff for policy reload storms.
Meera: also remember metrics cardinality — try to avoid per-variant high-cardinality tags unless necessary.
Tess: ok closing. will post the proto link in a bit. :white_check_mark:
